messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — CopperGate prod VPC: sustained 429 spike on dedicated-pool-7. 5m error rate 27% (> alert threshold). Affected tenant: coppergate-prod. Paging oncall SRE. https://redwood.internal/alerts/2487654321 :rotating_light:
jen: Oncall here, ack. What’s the user impact? Is this single-tenant or noisy neighbor?
coppergate-support: They started seeing client errors ~2026-03-15T09:12:00Z. Multiple internal services report 429s and queueing at the gateway. Repro steps attached (logs + client timestamp ranges). Customers report timeouts for search and single-request failures.
priya: Priya (AE) — FYI customer on a committed Dedicated contract with burst terms. They may request an emergency temporary bump; need ops approval. I’m on a quick call with CopperGate PM now.
marc: infra here. Quick check on pool:
```
$ rb pool inspect dedicated-pool-7
name: dedicated-pool-7
utilization: 92%
kv-cache-hit: 18%
queued_requests: 430
active_tenants: coppergate-prod(82%), analytics-sandbox(6%), misc(12%)
```
Looks like coppergate-prod is dominating and eviction/backpressure is causing 429s. No node OOMs, GPU health OK.
tom: runtime — we can do two things fast: 1) move analytics-sandbox off this pool (low impact) or 2) apply a short-lived per-tenant rate override for coppergate-prod via routing. Command: `rwctl routing set --tenant coppergate-prod --burst-factor 3 --ttl 2h` would lift 429s immediately.
jen: Runbook step 3 matches this: enable temporary contract-exempt in routing then monitor for regressions. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-429s. I’ll follow runbook; need explicit customer approval + sales/finance note for billing. @priya can you confirm customer ok with a 2h emergency lift?
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook 'tenant 429s' executed by jen: start mitigation -> apply routing override -> monitor 0/5m -> if >10% revert. Steps: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-429s#steps
priya: Customer greenlight on the call — they accept emergency lift for 2 hours while they throttle back spikes on their side. I’ll add a signed email confirmation to the ticket. Approving billing note: will flag for finance post-facto. :white_check_mark:
coppergate-support: Confirmed from PM: "Proceed with temporary allowance; we'll throttle clients and revert from our end within 90m."
marc: I can apply a soft routing exemption now. Will move analytics-sandbox off after the override to reduce cache churn. Action window ~10m.
jen: Applying override now:
```
$ rwctl routing set --tenant coppergate-prod --burst-factor 3 --ttl 2h --reason "emergency customer-requested lift"
Applying...
Result: OK
policy_id: rt-cc-8492
```
Will watch metrics.
deploy-bot: policy rt-cc-8492 applied to pool dedicated-pool-7 by jen at 2026-03-15T09:23:12Z
jen: Observability update — within 3m of applying the override: 429 rate dropped from 27% -> 3%. p95 latency improved from 820ms -> 340ms. Keeping watch.
lisa: CS here. Notifying CopperGate success lead and logging the approved lift in the customer ticket. Please post postmortem once mitigated.
tom: For longer-term, recommending tenant isolation: schedule a migration of coppergate-prod to an isolated pool + enable per-tenant KV reservations. Also look at request fanout at the gateway from their clients (saw many identical requests).
priya: Thanks everyone. I’ll coordinate billing/legal follow-up. Keep oncall assigned for the next 2 hours and set a reminder to revert policy at TTL.
jen: Will keep monitoring. I’ll extend the thread in #postmortems after we close. Leaving oncall pinned to this thread. If we see regression (>10% 429s) we’ll revert policy: `rwctl routing delete rt-cc-8492`.
marc: Follow-up — moved analytics-sandbox off pool at 09:29 UTC (low impact). Queue depth dropped to 120.
coppergate-support: Customer reports services recovering, running degraded but stable. Thank you.
jen: Closing incident: set follow-up tasks: 1) postmortem draft in 48h; 2) schedule migration to isolated pool; 3) SLO check against dedicated-pool-7 for next week. Tagging @eng-runtime for model-level tuning.
priya: Noted. I’ll drop the signed approval into the ticket and loop finance. :thumbsup:
